files.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand / precise graphic identity edit.
Edit target: the attached white-on-black twin-face mark chosen by the user for their personal homepage Little Stone Still Here. This is the SELECTED DIRECTION. Refine this exact emblem, not a different logo. Keep its recognizable two facing profiles which together also read as one frontal face. Keep the broad, gently rounded paired head silhouettes, the near-symmetrical balance, the two minimal eye cutouts, white ink and black background, and the overall compact proportions.

The ONE major change is the CENTRAL NEGATIVE SPACE, including only the inner lip/chin contours necessary to form it.
Present problem: the black almond-shaped mouth cavity and narrow straight black neck below it look like a mask or a goblet. Rebuild that area as an inviting OPEN PASSAGE between two people. Shape a single calm continuous black space from the lower edge toward the narrow space between their noses. At the bottom it is generously open to the surrounding background, then it naturally narrows as it leads upward between them. The inner lower jaw/neck silhouettes should taper gently away from each other toward the bottom, allowing this passage to open. Remove the abrupt wide oval bulb and straight bottle stem. Preserve just enough minimal lip/chin inflection above the passage to keep the two profile faces legible, without literal kiss-shaped protrusions.
The path should have a subtle, graceful organic inflection, not a rigid road diagram or a drawn letter. Use simple restrained continuous curves with optically balanced positive white masses. The negative space itself is the path: do not draw a separate road, line or doorway over the design. No perspective surface, no road markings, no doorframe, no house roof, no arch added as an icon. No tiny stone or new decorative object in the center. Keep the center as EMPTY BLACK SPACE.

Concept expressed through shape: the two people define a place to meet. The visitor approaches through what the author has left, and the whole only becomes a face when both are perceived together. Author, visitor, and the space between them. The homepage is a place you can approach and remain; the dark gap should visibly belong to the surrounding space, rather than be a sealed hole. The Pink Floyd Division Bell lineage of the source must remain clear.

Render ONE very simple finished-looking 2D main-logo candidate, flat uniform pure white on pure black, crisp graphic contours, tiny corner softening, gentle and restrained rather than squishy. Same single-logo centered square composition as input, generous blank margin. No lettering, no LSSH, no caption, no explanation, no diagram, no variants, no mockups, no gradients, no bevels, no shading or textures. Preserve the selected identity while making its figure-ground relationship more purposeful and inviting.

Input reference role: the attached The Wall album artwork is a LETTERING STYLE REFERENCE ONLY. Use its distinctive Pink Floyd handwritten letterforms and composition as the direct basis for a new personal-site wordmark.
Create exactly this two-line wordmark, all lowercase, with this line break:
little stone
still here

These are the ONLY words to appear. No uppercase initial letters. Do not write Pink Floyd, The Wall, LSSH or anything else.
Reinterpret the reference's spontaneous, lyrical hand-drawn ink rhythm in lowercase: varied letter heights, slightly leaning stems, confident quick strokes, a few expressive tapered exits, lively but measured spacing. Retain the recognizably hand-lettered Pink Floyd / The Wall character, while tempering its sharpest aggression to be gentle and intimate. Think a considered personal inscription, not a commercial typeface. Individual characters must be very legible, especially the double t in little and the double l in still. Hand-drawn construction, NOT standard cursive script, NOT generic geometric sans, NOT rounded bubble letters. Do not make every letter connected. Avoid chaotic crossings, ornamental flourishes, swashes, long underlines, or scratched distressed texture.
The two lines should form one balanced centered wordmark. First line naturally wider; second line centered below with comfortable but compact line spacing, long stems must not collide. Similar letter height and stroke weight in both lines. Stroke width should be substantial enough to remain visible below a bold main symbol.
Pure flat white lettering on pure flat black square canvas, absolutely no gradient, shadow, texture, paper, brick pattern, background illustration or material rendering. No face, prism, icon or other imagery. One single two-line wordmark centered with generous margin, width about 72 percent of image. This asset will be paired below the chosen two-face logo later.
